A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same survey, with readable text, equations, three figures, Table 1, and references. All 25 pages of each were inspected; neither includes a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 synthesizes prior research without reporting original experimental, simulation, user-study, or empirical data-analysis results. Its numerical findings are attributed to cited studies; its figures and table are conceptual.

after.justification: v2 retains the survey format and findings attributed to prior studies. It introduces no original empirical results.

M1.justification: The Peirce-based framework and descriptions of methods in Sections 4–7 are unchanged. No algorithm, model component, or procedure is introduced or revised.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts original training or evaluation, and the benchmark and task descriptions in Sections 4–7 are unchanged. The citation replacement in Section 6 does not establish different evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Both versions discuss the same methods and reported comparisons from prior research. Neither contains an original baseline evaluation, and no comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Descriptions of benchmark sizes, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures are retained. No evaluation protocol or experimental setting is added or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version reports original ablation or robustness experiments. The illustrative cases and descriptions of analyses from prior studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: There are no changes to repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical procedures. Section 6 retains the same five-annotator description despite changing its source citation.

E6.justification: The numerical and qualitative findings summarized from prior work are unchanged. Section 6 still reports disagreement in 62.34% of 1,365 explanations assessed by five annotators; only the attribution changes.

T1.justification: The logical formulations of hypothesis generation, application, and validation in Sections 4–6 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and summary retain the same contribution: organizing hypothesis discovery around abduction, deduction, and induction, and advocating integrated, realistic discovery benchmarks.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations concerning natural versus formal language, unreliable evaluation, hypothesis leakage, and restricted simulation environments are unchanged. The Section 6 citation replacement leaves its argument about validation ambiguity intact.

D1.justification: No implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, or code/data-access instructions are added or revised. The new OpenReview link supplies review metadata rather than experimental reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 6 reattributes the annotator-disagreement finding from Zhang et al. (2020), WinoWhy, to Zhao et al. (2023), which was already cited elsewhere. The WinoWhy bibliography entry is removed; the broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds publication-status and OpenReview text and updates the arXiv header. Apart from the citation substitution, the main wording, terminology, and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The running publication header and first-page review line alter spacing and pagination, including moving the start of Section 2 from page 2 to page 3. Figures 1–3 and Table 1 retain their content, captions, and designs.

improvement.justification: The substantive survey and visual explanations are unchanged; the publication metadata and reflow provide no clear overall quality gain. The potentially consequential edit is Section 6's source reassignment, but the supplied PDFs do not establish which citation correctly supports the retained disagreement statistic. Its effect on scholarly accuracy, and therefore the net quality direction, remains uncertain.
